title: Introduction — What Is the Rapture?
summary: Start with the core biblical event before comparing interpretations.

pretrib.short: Pre-tribulation Christians affirm a literal catching away of the church before the final Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: The rapture is understood as a distinct event in which Christ comes for His church before the Tribulation.

support.why: “Caught up” is read as the church being removed to meet Christ.
Jesus’ promise to receive believers is connected with the rapture.

adventist.short: Adventists affirm the catching up but identify it with Christ’s one visible Second Coming.
adventist.teaching: The resurrection, transformation, and catching up occur when Jesus returns visibly and gloriously.

support.why: Shout, archangel, trumpet, resurrection, and gathering occur together.
Christ’s return is visible to every eye.

bibleFirst: The catching up is explicit. The timing and whether it is separate from the visible Second Coming are interpretive questions.

title: Is the Rapture Secret?
summary: Does Scripture describe the event as invisible or silent?

pretrib.short: Pre-trib believers emphasize a sudden, unexpected removal of the church before the Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: “Secret rapture” usually emphasizes surprise and sudden disappearance, though not every teacher claims the event is literally silent.

support.why: The day comes like a thief in the night.
The unknown hour and one-taken/one-left language are used to support sudden removal.

adventist.short: Adventists reject a secret Second Coming and emphasize that Christ’s return is public, audible, and visible.
adventist.teaching: The shout, archangel’s voice, trumpet, resurrection, and every-eye language are understood as a public event.

support.why: The passage includes conspicuous sounds and resurrection.

bibleFirst: Suddenness is explicit. Invisibility is not stated in 1 Thessalonians 4.

title: Does the Church Escape the Great Tribulation?
summary: Removal before the crisis versus preservation through it.

pretrib.short: The church is removed before the Tribulation because believers are not appointed to wrath.
pretrib.teaching: The final Tribulation is viewed as a distinct period of divine judgment from which the church is removed beforehand.

support.why: “Keep thee from the hour” is interpreted as removal from the coming worldwide test.
Believers are not appointed to wrath.

adventist.short: God’s people pass through the final crisis but are protected and delivered.
adventist.teaching: Adventists distinguish tribulation from divine wrath and understand God as preserving His people through the crisis.

support.why: The elect are gathered after the tribulation.
God’s people are present in the time of trouble and are delivered.

bibleFirst: Deliverance from wrath is explicit. Removal before tribulation is an interpretation.

title: One Taken, One Left

pretrib.short: The one taken is often understood as a believer removed in the rapture.
pretrib.teaching: The sudden separation is read as believers being taken while unbelievers remain.

support.why: One is taken and the other left.

adventist.short: The Noah context is emphasized: the flood took the wicked away while Noah remained.
adventist.teaching: The immediate context makes it unsafe to assume that being taken automatically means raptured to heaven.

support.why: The flood took the wicked away.

bibleFirst: The main point is readiness because the hour is unknown.

title: Matthew 24 — The Gathering of the Elect

pretrib.short: This gathering is usually distinguished from the earlier rapture of the church.
pretrib.teaching: Many pre-trib interpreters understand this as Christ’s visible post-Tribulation return, not the church’s earlier rapture.

support.why: The gathered elect are understood as a different group/event from the church rapture.

adventist.short: This is understood as the same final gathering described by Paul.
adventist.teaching: Christ appears visibly, a trumpet sounds, and His people are gathered.

support.why: The sequence places the gathering after tribulation.

bibleFirst: The stated sequence is tribulation → visible Son of Man → trumpet → gathering.
